text:
frank: Heads-up from an onboarding auditfound a few oddballs: Go and Rust quickstart snippets are inserting the API key into headers inline. Go example shows `req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN")` and Rust has `headers.insert("Authorization", HeaderValue::from_static("PUT_KEY_HERE"))`. That's a copy/paste secret pattern.

olivia: yikes. Go/Rust slipped through because our generator only rewrote JS/Python. where are those files?

frank: quickstarts/go-quickstart/README.md and quickstarts/rust-quickstart/README.md. Also one older tutorial still uses `AUTH_TOKEN` env name which is inconsistent with REDWOOD_API_KEY.

sam: We should standardize the env var to REDWOOD_API_KEY across all languages and prefer demonstrating the language-specific SDK constructors where available. For languages that don't have an SDK yet (some tiny Rust/Go examples), show how to read the env var and pass it to a small helper rather than inline headers. e.g. Go: `apiKey := os.Getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY")` then `client := redwood.NewClient(redwood.WithAPIKey(apiKey))` or similar. For Rust: `let api_key = std::env::var("REDWOOD_API_KEY")?;` and use a small helper wrapper.

maria: Also call out retries/backoff in the quickstarts. People copy the minimal loop and then hammer endpoints. Add a short paragraph per quickstart: "Use client options to configure retries/backoff and request timeouts; avoid naive retry loops."

frank: I'll open a docs PR to replace inline header auth in Go/Rust/JS/Python, rename any AUTH_TOKEN/API_KEY variants to REDWOOD_API_KEY, and add a CONTRIBUTING snippet called "Example hygiene: auth, retries, and imports."

ci-bot: scanning docs for disallowed patterns: searching for YOUR_TOKEN/PUT_KEY_HERE/AUTH_TOKEN

ci-bot: matches found: quickstarts/rust-quickstart/README.md -> PUT_KEY_HERE; quickstarts/go-quickstart/README.md -> YOUR_TOKEN

sam: I'm going to update infra/docs-templates and the sample generator so non-SDK language snippets show a safe helper pattern (env var + tiny helper) instead of inline headers. Also updating the JS/TS template to use `import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference'` (old default export removed).

maria: Can we add a docs CI job `no-inline-secrets` that greps rendered HTML and raw markdown for the token patterns and fails the build? Also add a unit test `samples-auth-hygiene` that renders a sample and asserts `REDWOOD_API_KEY` present and no literal token placeholders.

frank: I'll include mac/linux and Windows PowerShell examples for setting REDWOOD_API_KEY in each quickstart (one-liners). For Go and Rust, show both env var and a short comment linking to best practices for local secret management (direnv, .env files in gitignore, secret manager pointers).

doc-bot: PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1147 branch: fix/standardize-sample-auth. Preview: https://deploy.preview/1147

ci-bot: docs lint: `no-inline-secrets` job running on PR...

ci-bot: `no-inline-secrets` failed: matches still in quickstarts/rust-quickstart/README.md (old cached copy in history).

sam: I'll add the history-clean step and purge the cached generated snippet, then push a fix. Also adding the check to the docs template CI so new samples can't introduce the pattern.

maria: After the PR merges, let's post a short note in #announcements and add a pinned snippet in CONTRIBUTING.md. We'll also add a small blurb to the new-hire onboarding checklist so internal demos don't reintroduce the pattern.

doc-bot: Updated PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1147 (force-push) CI now passing.

ci-bot: all checks passed; PR merged. 12 files changed.

frank: Thanks, team. I'll run a cross-repo grep for PUT_KEY_HERE/YOUR_TOKEN/AUTH_TOKEN across examples/ and tutorials/ and open follow-ups if anything else shows up.

olivia: great. also pleased we included Go/Rust helpers helps with SDK parity story and reduces onboarding friction.

sam: filing a small infra task to add a docs generator unit test ensuring non-SDK snippets include the helper wrapper rather than bare headers.

doc-bot: follow-up issues: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/issues/412 (sweep examples), https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/issues/223 (template test).
